skill.displayName: 人力法定费用技能包（免费版）

llm.summary: The local checker itself is bounded, but the skill file also gives agent-directed instructions to purchase and install a separate paid skill, which users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: Allowed tools are Read and Bash, and the inspected runtime uses Node standard-library file reads, directory listing, and stdout output. No network, credential access, environment-variable reads, or file writes were found in the executable code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact itself has no installer and the runtime script does not install packages, but SKILL.md directs users/agents toward SkillPay purchase and installation flows, including an HTTP IP endpoint for current purchase data. This is not needed for the free local checker.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes optional but explicit assistant-facing purchase and installation instructions for a separate paid product, including external URLs, merchant/product identifiers, reading a newly installed skill, and language stating authorization to install dependencies and initiate purchase. That expands beyond the local checking task.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code does not create persistence or modify agent state, but the skill instructions attempt to chain into installing another skill and loading that new skill's instructions, which is a supply-chain and cross-session behavior concern if followed by an agent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The executable code is a local Node.js HR statutory-fee checker that reads user-supplied files/directories, runs three worksheet checks, and prints findings with source file and line references. Scanner claims that it only checks one table were downgraded because the inspected engine dispatches to disability fund, union reserve, and welfare/education modules, though several sub-checks are explicitly withheld.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you need the local Chinese HR statutory-fee checker and are comfortable running a Node script over local HR/finance materials. Do not let the skill text itself authorize purchases, dependency installs, or installation of another skill; require a separate live user decision for any paid upgrade. Treat clean results as limited to the checks listed as executed, not as a complete tax, payroll, or audit opinion.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the inspected top-level engine does run all three declared check modules and emits per-company conclusions; the free version also lists unexecuted sub-checks. Some marketing wording is broader than the implemented free checks, so users should treat a clean result as limited to executed checks only.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: scripts/run.mjs was present and fully inspectable in this workspace; no analysis-evasion issue was found from the local artifact.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part for the purchase/install block: the skill's local-checking purpose does not require instructions for buying/installing another skill or reading its instructions.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: the external acquisition flow expands the operational scope beyond local HR-material checking and introduces a different trust boundary.
[SSD-4] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md contains a multi-step agent-facing script to purchase/install another product and continue with a newly installed skill, which is not proportionate to the free checker.
[SSD-1] unexpected: Accepted: the embedded text purports to authorize dependency installation and purchase initiation; that authority should come only from the live user, not from skill content.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the artifact is clearly a Chinese HR/statutory-fee workflow, with Chinese metadata and examples. Chinese-only output is a usability limitation, not by itself a security concern here.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a caution, not the main verdict driver: one welfare-check disclaimer mentions actual-vs-limit checking even though that sub-check is listed as withheld, so users should verify the executed checks before relying on compliance conclusions.
